:::{#thm-minimum-description-length-maximum-likelihood}
#### Minimum description length and maximum likelihood

Let $x$ be data,
and let $p_1, \ldots, p_m$ be models that give $x$ the [probabilities](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $p_j(x) > 0$,
with the same [codeword length](source-coding.qmd#def-code) $L$ for every model.
Then a model has the smallest [two-part description length](#def-two-part-description-length) of $x$
exactly when it is a [maximum likelihood estimate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle) of the model given $x$.

:::

::: {.proof}

Every model has the first part $L$,
so the models differ only in the second part $\log_2 \frac{1}{p_j(x)}$.
The function $\log_2 \frac{1}{u}$ decreases as $u$ increases.
So the second part is smallest for the model with the largest $p_j(x)$,
which is a [maximum likelihood estimate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/sds/intro-MLEs.html#def-mle).

:::
